lines.text: I had been gone a month. Tobin had been home for half of it. That was apparently long enough to build a bathhouse.
Hot water, my lord! Lighthouse glass heats it. Hot water all day, all winter, for everyone. The first hot bath north of the Senn!
Ten years I've waited for a hot bath. Ten years. I may never get out.
Hot water is for soup. I've washed in a cold bucket for fifty years.
Yes, Bram. We can tell.
The war of the bathhouse lasted four days. Bram poured cold water in. Oswin poured hot water in. Tobin rebuilt the boiler twice.
It ended when Ash jumped in. Nobody won. Everybody got wet.
Then something stranger happened. One of our diggers had crushed two fingers at Saltmouth. Granny held his hand in the warm water to wash it.
Well. That's new.
The swelling went down while we watched. Granny had been setting bones in Greyhollow for sixty years. She had never set one in a minute.
Root aether. Farmer's aether, the nobles call it. Healer's aether, more like. And it seems to love warm water.
By the end of the week, four more of our Root folk had found the same gift in the bath. Granny called them her apprentices. They called her terrifying.
Our school started on a steamed-up window. My six wards, one finger each, and the letters of their own names.
On the third night, Tobin joined them. He had dug his grandfather's old forge-book out of a chest while he was hunting for boiler plans.
Sixty years of secrets in here, my lord. And I can't read a single word.
That same night, Ash came and fetched me. He had chosen the warmest room in Greyhollow for her. The bathhouse boiler room.
Three pups. Two of them squirming. The smallest wasn't moving at all.
Don't name them, Lucan. A name is a whole claim poured out in one breath. Three of them, on top of everything you carry? It will cost you.
I named the first one Rook, because he was black as one. The second was Birk, for birch bark.
The third was small and very still, like a little mountain lake.
You're mine now. Your name is Tarn.
She sneezed. Then she squeaked. Then I fell over.
I slept for two days. When I woke up, all three of them were asleep on my chest.
Absolutely not.
Meanwhile, Tobin had learned his first word. He showed me the next morning. It was written under a drawing of a sword.
Glass.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter forty-eight, coming soon.
